title: Routing seam request contract (caller -> routing authority)
description: The frozen INPUT half of the routing seam (issue #426, ADR-0015). The caller asks the routing authority for a decision about one unit of work; the authority is gateway/sme-routing (the RoutingPolicy port implementation), which owns every decision and policy field on the other side of this seam. Every field here is written by exactly one side: the caller. Field names align with the live authority where one exists (task_type is the router's task 'type'; complexity is the router's 0..100 'complexity'; tier is the tier the caller requests or floors at). See docs/contracts/routing/README.md and docs/decision-records/ADR-0015-routing-seam-single-authority.md.

task_type.description: The kind of work, used to select a route. The live authority reads this as the router task 'type' and resolves it against the declared route-policy dispatch_defaults / tier-policy task_overrides (doc_update, audit, script_fix, config_change, code_review, ...). An undeclared type takes the declared fail-safe route; it is never silently cheap.

complexity.description: The caller's 0..100 difficulty estimate for the work. The authority compares it against the declared complexity_to_tier bands; the caller never picks the tier from it (the band map is a policy field the authority owns).

capability.description: The capability the work requires (the registry capability id, e.g. code-author, test-author, research, docs-authoring). Capability resolution selects the worker; it is an input to the decision, not a field the caller may resolve to a tier itself.

tier.description: The tier the caller requests or floors at. The request is a floor, never a ceiling: the authority may raise it (escalation, security/IaC floor) but never silently lower it below the declared floor. The effective tier is the authority's output field 'tier' in routing-decision.schema.json.
